newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan market plans three financial futures.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan market plans three financial futures.

text.p: Taiwan's futures exchange will offer local stock index, exchange rate and interest rate futures once it opens in October, official media quoted the head of the Securities and Futures Commission as saying on Friday.

Commission chairman Lu Daung-yen voiced confidence that in view of the huge turnover in Taiwan's main stock market, the three financial futures would ensure healthy development of the exchange, the state-funded Central News Agency said.
"The Taiwan stock market's recent turnover has ranked as the world's second largest," Lu said. "Such a strong physical market provides a basis for a prosperous futures market outlook."
Taiwan's daily stock exchange turnover has regularly topped T$200 billion (US$7 billion), spiking to an all-time high T$251 billion on June 19.
Friday's T$233 billion was the second highest on record.
Regulators have pledged to open Taiwan's long-awaited -- and repeatedly delayed -- futures exchange on October 1.
Taiwan investors currently are banned from trading offshore futures contracts directly linked to Taiwan's stock performance, although that prohibition will be lifted from August 1.
Taiwan stock-index futures were launched over Taipei's objections on January 9 by the Singapore International Monetary Exchange and the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.

Establishment of Taiwan's first futures exchange has been planned for years and organisers had set a launch target of July, but the opening was delayed by legislative wrangling and regulatory red tape.
